Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd F. Hoffmann-La Roche Ltd Updated Phase Ib/IIa Brainshuttle™ AD study data for trontinemab demonstrating rapid amyloid removal dynamics and changes in key biomarkers Phase III PrevenTRON study design specifics for trontinemab in preclinical Alzheimer’s disease, which has commenced enrolment Phase II TARBELA-AD study design for the investigational oral NLRP3 inhibitor RG6434 in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, representing a novel mechanism of action targeting neuroinflammation Global clinical and health economic data on the Elecsys ® pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181 blood tests supporting accessible, timely diagnosis Basel, 10 November 2026 - Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today that it will present new data across its pharmaceuticals and diagnostics portfolios at the 19 th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) Congress, taking place in Boston, MA, from 16–19 November 2026. Across 16 accepted abstracts, including two scientific symposia and two oral presentations, Roche will highlight its differentiated approach to neurodegeneration: uniting high-accuracy diagnostic testing with targeted investigational therapeutics to address the disease across its continuum. Expanding its Alzheimer’s disease pipeline, Roche is initiating a new Phase II clinical trial, TARBELA-AD, evaluating an investigational oral NLRP3 inhibitor, RG6434, in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease. The study underscores Roche's multi-pronged strategy to target distinct biological mechanisms, investigating neuroinflammation as a critical driver of pathology alongside amyloid aggregation. “Amyloid clearance remains a vital foundation, but halting a disease as complex as Alzheimer’s demands multifaceted and complementary strategies," said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. "By advancing our Phase II TARBELA-AD trial evaluating an NLRP3 inhibitor, alongside ongoing trontinemab programmes, we will test additional therapeutic hypotheses to potentially stop or prevent disease progression." Roche’s diagnostics division continues to expand access to earlier and more accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer’s through its comprehensive blood-based biomarker portfolio, including the approved Elecsys ® pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181 tests. “Transforming care for Alzheimer’s disease begins with bringing clarity to individuals and families as early as possible," said Matt Sause, CEO of Roche Diagnostics. "Elecsys pTau217 is the first and only FDA-cleared, single biomarker blood test that both rules in and rules out amyloid pathology. By expanding assessment into primary care as well as specialist settings, it can deliver fast, accurate answers so people can evaluate treatment and plan for the future." Pharmaceuticals Scientific symposia will feature the latest research on investigational trontinemab and NLRP3 inhibition: Monday 16 November 16:50-17:30 ET: “Visualizing the Brainshuttle™: Pioneering neuroimaging and mechanistic insights of amyloid clearance with trontinemab” will provide the latest neuroimaging, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics and safety data from the Phase Ib/IIa Brainshuttle ™ AD study, which is evaluating the potential of trontinemab to provide rapid and robust amyloid clearance in Alzheimer’s disease. Tuesday 17 November 14:35-15:15 ET: “Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer’s Disease: Targeting the NLRP3 Inflammasome and Neuroimmune Crosstalk” will explore neuroinflammation in Alzheimer’s disease and early data on targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome with RG6434. Keynote address by Geoff Kerchner, Global Head of Neurodegeneration Product Development at Roche: Tuesday 17 November 9:10-9:35 ET: “A glimpse of the future: How diagnostics, therapies, trials, and concepts of prevention must evolve” will explore the interplay between these themes to crystallise a vision for what the future could look like, and what we need to do now to realise it. An oral presentation will provide a deep dive into the Phase III PrevenTRON study of trontinemab in preclinical Alzheimer’s disease: Wednesday 18 November 9:55-10:05 ET: “PrevenTRON: Evaluating the effect of trontinemab in cognitively unimpaired individuals with biomarkers of Alzheimer’s disease at high risk of clinical decline” will detail the study design and participant screening for the PrevenTRON study, which has recently started enrolling participants. Diagnostics Across multiple posters, available to view from Monday 16 November at 9:00 ET, Roche will present new clinical, health economic and real-world data for its latest blood tests, including Elecsys pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181, across diverse global patient populations and care settings to support Alzheimer’s diagnosis. Key presentations will explore the impact of integrating blood-based pTau217 testing into routine clinical practice on healthcare economics and efficiency of diagnostic pathways. About Roche in Alzheimer’s For nearly 30 years, Roche has been working towards a day when we can detect and treat Alzheimer’s earlier, in order to slow, stop or even prevent its progression by combining our expertise across pharmaceuticals and diagnostics. Today, Roche’s Alzheimer’s disease portfolio spans investigational medicines targeting complementary biological pathways, from amyloid to neuroinflammation, with candidates such as trontinemab, nivegacetor and RG6434. Roche is also advancing innovative approaches to drug delivery through Brainshuttle™ technology, designed to enhance the transport of medicines across the blood–brain barrier. Its diagnostics division offers an industry-leading portfolio of approved products spanning cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) assays and blood-based tests, including Elecsys pTau181, pTau217 and ApoE4. Roche also maintains a comprehensive portfolio of research use only (RUO) tests, providing early access to new biomarkers to empower researchers to shape tomorrow’s diagnostics. Addressing the global burden of Alzheimer’s disease requires more than innovative tests and treatments. This is why Roche partners across the healthcare ecosystem with clinicians, scientists, patient advocates, policymakers and health systems to help simplify the care pathway and ensure advances in research translate into real-world benefits for millions worldwide. About Roche Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) is a healthcare company uniquely placed to prevent, stop and cure diseases by uniting leading science and technology across diagnostics, medicines and digital solutions. Roche was founded in Basel, Switzerland in 1896 and today is a leading provider of transformative medicines and diagnostics for millions of people in over 150 countries around the world. It is dedicated to tackling healthcare challenges that place the greatest strain on patients, families, communities and healthcare systems. Across its Diagnostics and Pharmaceutical divisions, Roche focuses on areas including oncology, neurology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, ophthalmology, infectious diseases and immunology with the aim of providing real and positive change for patients, the people they love and the professionals who care for them. Genentech in the United States is a fully owned subsidiary in the Roche Group. Roche is the majority shareholder in Chugai Pharmaceutical, a major innovator in the Japanese therapeutic antibody market. For more information, please visit www.roche.com . About Roche in Alzheimer’s For nearly 30 years, Roche has been working towards a day when we can detect and treat Alzheimer’s earlier, in order to slow, stop or even prevent its progression by combining our expertise across pharmaceuticals and diagnostics. Roche is also advancing innovative approaches to drug delivery through Brainshuttle™ technology, designed to enhance the transport of medicines across the blood–brain barrier. Updated Phase Ib/IIa Brainshuttle™ AD study data for trontinemab demonstrating rapid amyloid removal dynamics and changes in key biomarkers Phase III PrevenTRON study design specifics for trontinemab in preclinical Alzheimer’s disease, which has commenced enrolment Phase II TARBELA-AD study design for the investigational oral NLRP3 inhibitor RG6434 in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease, representing a novel mechanism of action targeting neuroinflammation Global clinical and health economic data on the Elecsys ® pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181 blood tests supporting accessible, timely diagnosis Basel, 10 November 2026 - Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today that it will present new data across its pharmaceuticals and diagnostics portfolios at the 19 th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) Congress, taking place in Boston, MA, from 16–19 November 2026. Across 16 accepted abstracts, including two scientific symposia and two oral presentations, Roche will highlight its differentiated approach to neurodegeneration: uniting high-accuracy diagnostic testing with targeted investigational therapeutics to address the disease across its continuum. Expanding its Alzheimer’s disease pipeline, Roche is initiating a new Phase II clinical trial, TARBELA-AD, evaluating an investigational oral NLRP3 inhibitor, RG6434, in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease. The study underscores Roche's multi-pronged strategy to target distinct biological mechanisms, investigating neuroinflammation as a critical driver of pathology alongside amyloid aggregation. “Amyloid clearance remains a vital foundation, but halting a disease as complex as Alzheimer’s demands multifaceted and complementary strategies," said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. "By advancing our Phase II TARBELA-AD trial evaluating an NLRP3 inhibitor, alongside ongoing trontinemab programmes, we will test additional therapeutic hypotheses to potentially stop or prevent disease progression." Roche’s diagnostics division continues to expand access to earlier and more accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer’s through its comprehensive blood-based biomarker portfolio, including the approved Elecsys ® pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181 tests. “Transforming care for Alzheimer’s disease begins with bringing clarity to individuals and families as early as possible," said Matt Sause, CEO of Roche Diagnostics. "Elecsys pTau217 is the first and only FDA-cleared, single biomarker blood test that both rules in and rules out amyloid pathology. By expanding assessment into primary care as well as specialist settings, it can deliver fast, accurate answers so people can evaluate treatment and plan for the future." Basel, 10 November 2026 - Roche (SIX: RO, ROP; OTCQX: RHHBY) announced today that it will present new data across its pharmaceuticals and diagnostics portfolios at the 19 th Clinical Trials on Alzheimer’s Disease (CTAD) Congress, taking place in Boston, MA, from 16–19 November 2026. Across 16 accepted abstracts, including two scientific symposia and two oral presentations, Roche will highlight its differentiated approach to neurodegeneration: uniting high-accuracy diagnostic testing with targeted investigational therapeutics to address the disease across its continuum.
th
Expanding its Alzheimer’s disease pipeline, Roche is initiating a new Phase II clinical trial, TARBELA-AD, evaluating an investigational oral NLRP3 inhibitor, RG6434, in early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease. The study underscores Roche's multi-pronged strategy to target distinct biological mechanisms, investigating neuroinflammation as a critical driver of pathology alongside amyloid aggregation.
“Amyloid clearance remains a vital foundation, but halting a disease as complex as Alzheimer’s demands multifaceted and complementary strategies," said Levi Garraway, M.D., Ph.D., Roche’s Chief Medical Officer and Head of Global Product Development. "By advancing our Phase II TARBELA-AD trial evaluating an NLRP3 inhibitor, alongside ongoing trontinemab programmes, we will test additional therapeutic hypotheses to potentially stop or prevent disease progression."
Roche’s diagnostics division continues to expand access to earlier and more accurate diagnosis of Alzheimer’s through its comprehensive blood-based biomarker portfolio, including the approved Elecsys ® pTau217 and Elecsys pTau181 tests.
“Transforming care for Alzheimer’s disease begins with bringing clarity to individuals and families as early as possible," said Matt Sause, CEO of Roche Diagnostics. "Elecsys pTau217 is the first and only FDA-cleared, single biomarker blood test that both rules in and rules out amyloid pathology. By expanding assessment into primary care as well as specialist settings, it can deliver fast, accurate answers so people can evaluate treatment and plan for the future."

Accessibility: Skip TopNav CIDEB siRNA Normalizes Liver Fat and Improves Liver Injury Markers in MASLD Patients, as Highlighted at AASLD November 08, 2026 16:00 ET | Source: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Single administration of CIDEB siRNA resulted in rapid, deep and durable reductions in liver fat by up to 80% that were sustained through 36 weeks Data from first-in-human trial were shared in oral presentation at AASLD The Liver Meeting ® and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine Regeneron to host virtual “Regeneron Roundtable” investor event to discuss its MASH pipeline programs on Tuesday, November 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced the first results from a first-in-human trial that demonstrated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA rapidly normalized liver fat and improved liver injury markers in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with effects that were sustained through week 36. CIDEB siRNA is an investigational, first-in-class, liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that mimics the protective effect of rare mutations in the CIDEB gene, which were discovered by the Regeneron Genetics Center ® . The results were published by The New England Journal of Medicine and simultaneously presented in an oral session at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting ® 2026. “Prior advances in steatotic liver disease have begun to make a difference, but there is so much more progress to be made to help patients normalize liver fat and reverse liver damage,” said Jörg Täubel, M.D., F.F.P.M., F.E.S.C., Executive Chairman of Richmond Pharmacology, Visiting Professor at King’s College London, Honorary Senior Research Fellow at St. George’s University in London, President of The Association for Applied Human Pharmacology and a lead investigator for the trial. “These results show CIDEB siRNA resulted in rapid, deep and sustained reductions in liver fat with improvements in markers of liver injury. With effects out to 36 weeks that support the potential for twice-yearly dosing, alongside the safety profile, the findings highlight CIDEB siRNA as a promising new therapeutic for MASH and other steatotic liver diseases.” MASLD occurs when excess fat accumulates in the liver and encompasses a spectrum of conditions ranging from simple fatty liver to the more serious disease of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). MASH is a progressive, fibrotic liver disease that affects approximately 13 million U.S. adults, which is characterized by inflammation and cell damage that can lead to cirrhosis, liver transplant, liver cancer and death if not properly managed. Historical clinical trial data report that currently approved MASH therapies have reached mean liver fat reductions of 47-57% at approximately one year. 1,2 A first-in-human, Phase 1/2 trial evaluated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA at four dose levels (n=30 for CIDEB siRNA groups) versus placebo (n=10) in adults with MASLD. The primary goal of the trial was to evaluate safety and tolerability, with liver fat and markers of liver injury evaluated as secondary endpoints. Meta-analyses of clinical trials of patients with MASH indicate that the depth of liver fat reduction correlates with liver biopsy response (e.g., MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement), supporting changes in liver fat as an informative, early pharmacodynamic readout. Results for CIDEB siRNA recipients showed: 58-80% dose-dependent liver fat reductions at week 36 , which had deepened from the rapid 49-72% reductions at week 6 (as measured by magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction, MRI-PDFF). Mean decrease in the placebo group was 2.9% at week 36. Liver fat was normalized in a majority (62%) of CIDEB siRNA recipients at week 36 (defined as liver fat content under 5% by MRI-PDFF) versus none in the placebo group. Additionally, 93% had reductions of liver fat of ≥30%, a threshold linked to histological MASH resolution. Improvements were seen in markers of liver injury at early timepoints and sustained through week 36 , with reductions in mean levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) across all doses and directionally similar changes in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Overall rates of adverse events (AEs) were generally similar between the CIDEB siRNA and placebo groups. All AEs were mild or moderate in severity, except for a severe, serious event of hyperglycemia in a CIDEB siRNA -treated participant that was not attributed to study drug (instead later attributed to a diagnosis of adult-onset Type 1 diabetes). There were no trial discontinuations and no nausea or vomiting AEs reported in the CIDEB siRNA groups, addressing a key tolerability limitation associated with other therapies. Longer-term safety and histologic outcomes are being evaluated in multiple, ongoing trials, including Phase 2a , Phase 2b and Phase 3 trials that are now recruiting. Regeneron is also investigating additional drug candidates informed by human genetics for the treatment of steatotic liver diseases. The potential uses of CIDEB siRNA described above are investigational, and its safety and efficacy have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority. About the “Regeneron Roundtable” Investor Event Regeneron will host a virtual investor event to discuss its cardiometabolic and MASH pipeline programs on Tuesday, November 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET. This is the next webcast in an investor event series called the “Regeneron Roundtable,” intended to highlight programs from the company’s innovative investigational pipeline. Links to the webcast and to register via telephone may be accessed from the ‘Investors and Media’ page of Regeneron’s website at https://investor.regeneron.com/events-and-presentations . Upon registration, all telephone participants will receive a confirmation email detailing how to join the conference call, including the dial-in number, along with a unique passcode and registrant ID that can be used to access the call. A replay of the conference call and webcast will be archived on the company’s website for at least 30 days. About CIDEB siRNA , the trial and the Regeneron MASLD/MASH Program CIDEB siRNA is an investigational, first-in-class, liver-targeted siRNA therapeutic that targets a receptor exclusively expressed in the liver to mimic the protective effect of naturally occurring loss-of-function and missense CIDEB mutations in a broad population of people with MASLD and MASH. The ongoing Phase 1/2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial is evaluating the safety and tolerability of CIDEB siRNA in adult participants with MASLD and MASH. The primary goal of the trial is to evaluate safety and tolerability with efficacy evaluated as a secondary endpoint through measures such as change in liver fat fraction by MRI-PDFF. Scientists at the Regeneron Genetics Center ® (RGC) analyzed genetic data to discover and/or validate genetic variants in the CIDEB and other genes that are associated with liver disease risk. Building on these findings, Regeneron collaborated with Alnylam to generate an siRNA targeting CIDEB and has the exclusive rights for the development of and commercialization of CIDEB siRNA ; Alnylam receives milestone and royalty payments. About Regeneron Regeneron (NASDAQ: REGN) is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops and commercializes life-transforming medicines for people with serious diseases. Founded and led by physician-scientists, our unique ability to repeatedly and consistently translate science into medicine has led to numerous approved treatments and product candidates in development, most of which were homegrown in our laboratories. Our medicines and pipeline are designed to help patients with eye diseases, allergic and inflammatory diseases, cancer, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurological diseases, hematologic conditions, infectious diseases, and rare diseases. Regeneron pushes the boundaries of scientific discovery and accelerates drug development using our proprietary technologies, such as VelociSuite ® , which produces optimized fully human antibodies and new classes of bispecific antibodies. We are shaping the next frontier of medicine with data-powered insights from the Regeneron Genetics Center ® and pioneering genetic medicine platforms, enabling us to identify innovative targets and complementary approaches to potentially treat or cure diseases. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Single administration of CIDEB siRNA resulted in rapid, deep and durable reductions in liver fat by up to 80% that were sustained through 36 weeks Data from first-in-human trial were shared in oral presentation at AASLD The Liver Meeting ® and simultaneously published in The New England Journal of Medicine Regeneron to host virtual “Regeneron Roundtable” investor event to discuss its MASH pipeline programs on Tuesday, November 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced the first results from a first-in-human trial that demonstrated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA rapidly normalized liver fat and improved liver injury markers in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with effects that were sustained through week 36. CIDEB siRNA is an investigational, first-in-class, liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that mimics the protective effect of rare mutations in the CIDEB gene, which were discovered by the Regeneron Genetics Center ® . The results were published by The New England Journal of Medicine and simultaneously presented in an oral session at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting ® 2026. “Prior advances in steatotic liver disease have begun to make a difference, but there is so much more progress to be made to help patients normalize liver fat and reverse liver damage,” said Jörg Täubel, M.D., F.F.P.M., F.E.S.C., Executive Chairman of Richmond Pharmacology, Visiting Professor at King’s College London, Honorary Senior Research Fellow at St. George’s University in London, President of The Association for Applied Human Pharmacology and a lead investigator for the trial. “These results show CIDEB siRNA resulted in rapid, deep and sustained reductions in liver fat with improvements in markers of liver injury. With effects out to 36 weeks that support the potential for twice-yearly dosing, alongside the safety profile, the findings highlight CIDEB siRNA as a promising new therapeutic for MASH and other steatotic liver diseases.” MASLD occurs when excess fat accumulates in the liver and encompasses a spectrum of conditions ranging from simple fatty liver to the more serious disease of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). MASH is a progressive, fibrotic liver disease that affects approximately 13 million U.S. adults, which is characterized by inflammation and cell damage that can lead to cirrhosis, liver transplant, liver cancer and death if not properly managed. Historical clinical trial data report that currently approved MASH therapies have reached mean liver fat reductions of 47-57% at approximately one year. 1,2 A first-in-human, Phase 1/2 trial evaluated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA at four dose levels (n=30 for CIDEB siRNA groups) versus placebo (n=10) in adults with MASLD. The primary goal of the trial was to evaluate safety and tolerability, with liver fat and markers of liver injury evaluated as secondary endpoints. Meta-analyses of clinical trials of patients with MASH indicate that the depth of liver fat reduction correlates with liver biopsy response (e.g., MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement), supporting changes in liver fat as an informative, early pharmacodynamic readout. Results for CIDEB siRNA recipients showed: 58-80% dose-dependent liver fat reductions at week 36 , which had deepened from the rapid 49-72% reductions at week 6 (as measured by magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction, MRI-PDFF). Mean decrease in the placebo group was 2.9% at week 36. Liver fat was normalized in a majority (62%) of CIDEB siRNA recipients at week 36 (defined as liver fat content under 5% by MRI-PDFF) versus none in the placebo group. Additionally, 93% had reductions of liver fat of ≥30%, a threshold linked to histological MASH resolution. Improvements were seen in markers of liver injury at early timepoints and sustained through week 36 , with reductions in mean levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) across all doses and directionally similar changes in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. Overall rates of adverse events (AEs) were generally similar between the CIDEB siRNA and placebo groups. All AEs were mild or moderate in severity, except for a severe, serious event of hyperglycemia in a CIDEB siRNA -treated participant that was not attributed to study drug (instead later attributed to a diagnosis of adult-onset Type 1 diabetes). There were no trial discontinuations and no nausea or vomiting AEs reported in the CIDEB siRNA groups, addressing a key tolerability limitation associated with other therapies. Longer-term safety and histologic outcomes are being evaluated in multiple, ongoing trials, including Phase 2a , Phase 2b and Phase 3 trials that are now recruiting. Regeneron is also investigating additional drug candidates informed by human genetics for the treatment of steatotic liver diseases. The potential uses of CIDEB siRNA described above are investigational, and its safety and efficacy have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority. TARRYTOWN, N.Y., Nov.  08, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: REGN) today announced the first results from a first-in-human trial that demonstrated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA rapidly normalized liver fat and improved liver injury markers in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) with effects that were sustained through week 36. CIDEB siRNA is an investigational, first-in-class, liver-targeted small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutic that mimics the protective effect of rare mutations in the CIDEB gene, which were discovered by the Regeneron Genetics Center ® . The results were published by The New England Journal of Medicine and simultaneously presented in an oral session at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting ® 2026.
CIDEB
discovered
published
“Prior advances in steatotic liver disease have begun to make a difference, but there is so much more progress to be made to help patients normalize liver fat and reverse liver damage,” said Jörg Täubel, M.D., F.F.P.M., F.E.S.C., Executive Chairman of Richmond Pharmacology, Visiting Professor at King’s College London, Honorary Senior Research Fellow at St. George’s University in London, President of The Association for Applied Human Pharmacology and a lead investigator for the trial. “These results show CIDEB siRNA resulted in rapid, deep and sustained reductions in liver fat with improvements in markers of liver injury. With effects out to 36 weeks that support the potential for twice-yearly dosing, alongside the safety profile, the findings highlight CIDEB siRNA as a promising new therapeutic for MASH and other steatotic liver diseases.”
MASLD occurs when excess fat accumulates in the liver and encompasses a spectrum of conditions ranging from simple fatty liver to the more serious disease of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). MASH is a progressive, fibrotic liver disease that affects approximately 13 million U.S. adults, which is characterized by inflammation and cell damage that can lead to cirrhosis, liver transplant, liver cancer and death if not properly managed. Historical clinical trial data report that currently approved MASH therapies have reached mean liver fat reductions of 47-57% at approximately one year. 1,2
1,2
A first-in-human, Phase 1/2 trial evaluated a single subcutaneous dose of CIDEB siRNA at four dose levels (n=30 for CIDEB siRNA groups) versus placebo (n=10) in adults with MASLD. The primary goal of the trial was to evaluate safety and tolerability, with liver fat and markers of liver injury evaluated as secondary endpoints. Meta-analyses of clinical trials of patients with MASH indicate that the depth of liver fat reduction correlates with liver biopsy response (e.g., MASH resolution and fibrosis improvement), supporting changes in liver fat as an informative, early pharmacodynamic readout.
Results for CIDEB siRNA recipients showed:
58-80% dose-dependent liver fat reductions at week 36 , which had deepened from the rapid 49-72% reductions at week 6 (as measured by magnetic resonance imaging-proton density fat fraction, MRI-PDFF). Mean decrease in the placebo group was 2.9% at week 36. Liver fat was normalized in a majority (62%) of CIDEB siRNA recipients at week 36 (defined as liver fat content under 5% by MRI-PDFF) versus none in the placebo group. Additionally, 93% had reductions of liver fat of ≥30%, a threshold linked to histological MASH resolution. Improvements were seen in markers of liver injury at early timepoints and sustained through week 36 , with reductions in mean levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) across all doses and directionally similar changes in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels.

Overall rates of adverse events (AEs) were generally similar between the CIDEB siRNA and placebo groups. All AEs were mild or moderate in severity, except for a severe, serious event of hyperglycemia in a CIDEB siRNA -treated participant that was not attributed to study drug (instead later attributed to a diagnosis of adult-onset Type 1 diabetes). There were no trial discontinuations and no nausea or vomiting AEs reported in the CIDEB siRNA groups, addressing a key tolerability limitation associated with other therapies.
Longer-term safety and histologic outcomes are being evaluated in multiple, ongoing trials, including Phase 2a , Phase 2b and Phase 3 trials that are now recruiting. Regeneron is also investigating additional drug candidates informed by human genetics for the treatment of steatotic liver diseases.

The potential uses of CIDEB siRNA described above are investigational, and its safety and efficacy have not been evaluated by any regulatory authority.
About the “Regeneron Roundtable” Investor Event Regeneron will host a virtual investor event to discuss its cardiometabolic and MASH pipeline programs on Tuesday, November 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET. This is the next webcast in an investor event series called the “Regeneron Roundtable,” intended to highlight programs from the company’s innovative investigational pipeline.

About CIDEB siRNA , the trial and the Regeneron MASLD/MASH Program CIDEB siRNA is an investigational, first-in-class, liver-targeted siRNA therapeutic that targets a receptor exclusively expressed in the liver to mimic the protective effect of naturally occurring loss-of-function and missense CIDEB mutations in a broad population of people with MASLD and MASH.
About CIDEB
, the trial and the Regeneron MASLD/MASH Program
The ongoing Phase 1/2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial is evaluating the safety and tolerability of CIDEB siRNA in adult participants with MASLD and MASH. The primary goal of the trial is to evaluate safety and tolerability with efficacy evaluated as a secondary endpoint through measures such as change in liver fat fraction by MRI-PDFF.
Scientists at the Regeneron Genetics Center ® (RGC) analyzed genetic data to discover and/or validate genetic variants in the CIDEB and other genes that are associated with liver disease risk. Building on these findings, Regeneron collaborated with Alnylam to generate an siRNA targeting CIDEB and has the exclusive rights for the development of and commercialization of CIDEB siRNA ; Alnylam receives milestone and royalty payments.
About Regeneron Regeneron (NASDAQ: REGN) is a leading biotechnology company that invents, develops and commercializes life-transforming medicines for people with serious diseases. Founded and led by physician-scientists, our unique ability to repeatedly and consistently translate science into medicine has led to numerous approved treatments and product candidates in development, most of which were homegrown in our laboratories. Our medicines and pipeline are designed to help patients with eye diseases, allergic and inflammatory diseases, cancer, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurological diseases, hematologic conditions, infectious diseases, and rare diseases.
About Regeneron
Regeneron pushes the boundaries of scientific discovery and accelerates drug development using our proprietary technologies, such as VelociSuite ® , which produces optimized fully human antibodies and new classes of bispecific antibodies. We are shaping the next frontier of medicine with data-powered insights from the Regeneron Genetics Center ® and pioneering genetic medicine platforms, enabling us to identify innovative targets and complementary approaches to potentially treat or cure diseases.

Accessibility: Skip TopNav Crescent Biopharma Announces Grants of Inducement Awards November 03, 2026 16:15 ET | Source: Crescent Biopharma, Inc. Crescent Biopharma, Inc. WALTHAM, Mass., Nov.  03, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Crescent Biopharma , Inc. (“Crescent” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: CBIO), a clinical-stage biotechnology company dedicated to rapidly advancing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients, today announced that the independent Compensation Committee of its Board of Directors approved the grant of options to purchase an aggregate of 11,775 shares of the Company’s ordinary shares to one non-executive employee as an equity inducement award under the Crescent Biopharma, Inc. 2025 Employment Inducement Incentive Award Plan, as amended (the “Inducement Plan”). The options were approved on November 2, 2026 and were material to the employee's acceptance of employment with Crescent, in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The options were granted with a 10-year term and an exercise price equal to $12.91, the closing price per share of Crescent’s ordinary shares as reported by Nasdaq on November 2, 2026. The options granted to the employee shall vest and become exercisable as to one-fourth (1/4th) of the shares subject to the options on the first anniversary of the employee’s start date, and one-forty-eighth (1/48th) of the shares subject to the options shall vest and become exercisable monthly thereafter, subject to continuous service with Crescent through the applicable vesting dates. The options are subject to the terms of the Inducement Plan and the terms and conditions of an option agreement covering the applicable grant. About Crescent Biopharma Crescent Biopharma’s vision is to build a world leading oncology company bringing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients. The Company’s clinical-stage pipeline includes its lead program, a PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody, as well as novel antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). By leveraging multiple modalities and established targets, Crescent aims to rapidly advance potentially transformative therapies as single agents and as part of combination regimens to treat a range of solid tumors. Accessibility: Skip TopNav Bolt Biotherapeutics to Participate in Upcoming Conferences November 03, 2026 08:00 ET | Source: Bolt Biotherapeutics, Inc. Bolt Biotherapeutics, Inc. REDWOOD CITY, Calif., Nov.  03, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Bolt Biotherapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: BOLT) (“Bolt” or the “Company”), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering a new generation of half-life-extended multispecific antibodies designed to deliver best-in-disease therapies, today announced participation in two upcoming investor conferences. Sheila Gujrathi, M.D., Chief Strategy Officer of Bolt and Co-Founder and former Chief Executive Officer of Prana Therapies, will deliver a company presentation, followed by a fireside chat, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 10:40 a.m. ET at the Stifel 2026 Healthcare Conference , and attend Jefferies Global Healthcare Conference in London , taking place November 16–19, 2026. In October 2026 , Bolt acquired Prana Therapies in a stock-for-stock reverse merger alongside a $120 million private placement financing, with the potential for up to an additional $60 million upon exercise of accompanying warrants. Following the acquisition, Bolt is primarily focused on advancing Prana’s pipeline of next-generation, half-life-extended multispecific antibodies, led by PRA-216, which is currently in Phase 2 development across multiple inflammatory diseases. Members of the management team will host one-on-one investor meetings during the conferences. A live webcast of the Stifel presentation will be available on the Events and Presentations section of Bolt’s website at https://investors.boltbio.com/news-and-events/events-and-presentations , with an archived replay accessible following the event date. About Bolt Biotherapeutics, Inc. Bolt Biotherapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering a new generation of half-life-extended multispecific antibodies designed to deliver best-in-disease therapies. Through the proprietary INSPIRE platform it acquired from Prana Therapies, the company combines complementary therapeutic mechanisms in fully IgG-based molecules designed for differentiated efficacy, extended exposure, and convenient dosing. The company’s lead program, PRA-216, is a novel IL-4Rα/TSLP bispecific antibody currently in Phase 2 development in asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and atopic dermatitis, with a fourth Phase 2 study planned in eosinophilic esophagitis. In addition to PRA-216, Bolt Biotherapeutics is advancing a wholly owned pipeline of additional INSPIRE-based multispecific programs across diseases with significant unmet need. Bolt’s pipeline also includes BDC-4182, a claudin 18.2-targeting Boltbody™ ISAC. For more information, please visit https://www.boltbio.com/ . articles.text:
Accessibility: Skip TopNav Shattuck Labs Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Recent Business Highlights November 05, 2026 08:00 ET | Source: Shattuck Labs, Inc. Shattuck Labs, Inc. – Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in Crohn’s disease; 12-week induction data expected in the first half of 2028 – – Announced RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in hidradenitis suppurativa; trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 – – Presented preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from a chronic toxicology study in non-human primates – AUSTIN, Texas and DURHAM, N.C., Nov.  05, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shattuck Labs, Inc. (Shattuck or the Company) (NASDAQ: STTK), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potential first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided recent business highlights. “We are very excited to begin Phase 2 clinical development with SL-325 in both Crohn’s disease and hidradenitis suppurativa. We believe these two studies will allow direct comparisons with the TL1A antibody class and evaluate the efficacy that may be left on the table due to the potential immunogenicity liabilities of TL1A antibodies,” said Taylor Schreiber, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Shattuck. “In addition, SL-846 has demonstrated a compelling profile in preclinical studies, and we expect to share initial Phase 1 clinical data for what we expect to be a first-in-class DR3 by IL-23 receptor blocking antibody in 2027.” DR3 Program Development in 2026 Shattuck is advancing a pipeline of DR3-targeted monoclonal and bispecific antibody product candidates for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Recent updates and anticipated upcoming milestones include: SL-325 Shattuck’s lead clinical-stage product candidate, SL-325, is a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody for the treatment of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), and other inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Phase 1 clinical trial results demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability, potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity with an antidrug antibody rate of 3.7%, and highly durable inhibition of TL1A binding to DR3 that may enable quarterly maintenance dosing. Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate three dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 232 patients, randomized 1:1:1:1. Primary endpoint is endoscopic response at 12 weeks. These data are expected in the first half of 2028. Announced plans to initiate the RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa, with trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. HS is the second Phase 2 indication for SL-325 and expands development beyond IBD. Submitted an Investigational New Drug (IND) application to the FDA in October 2026. Designed RECEPTIVE-HS1 as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating two dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 150 patients, randomized 1:1:1. Primary endpoint is HiSCR50 response at Week 16, with data expected in the first half of 2028. Appointed Shoba Ravichandran, M.D., as Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, to lead the clinical development of SL-325 in HS. Dr. Ravichandran brings more than 20 years of drug development experience, including leading the global approval of Cosentyx in HS at Novartis. SL-846 Shattuck’s lead bispecific product candidate, SL-846, is a potentially first-in-class, half-life extended DR3 x IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking antibody for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Presented preliminary preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from the GLP toxicology study in non-human primates, which showed the following: Well tolerated through the top dose of 100 mg/kg. No evidence of DR3 or IL-23R agonism. Full and durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3, and complete blockade of IL-23 signaling. Data from the NHP study support potential quarterly subcutaneous dosing in humans. NHP and in silico analyses suggest that SL-846 may have a superior immunogenicity profile to TL1A directed bispecific antibodies; projected human anti-drug antibody rate of between 8-12%. Shattuck expects to initiate a Phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial of SL-846 and report initial data in 2027. Upcoming Events Shattuck plans to participate in the following upcoming events. Details will be included on the Events & Presentations section of the Company’s website. Evercore ISI 9th Annual Healthcare Conference, November 30-December 1, 2026 . Shattuck Labs, Inc. – Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in Crohn’s disease; 12-week induction data expected in the first half of 2028 – – Announced RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in hidradenitis suppurativa; trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 – – Presented preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from a chronic toxicology study in non-human primates – AUSTIN, Texas and DURHAM, N.C., Nov.  05, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shattuck Labs, Inc. (Shattuck or the Company) (NASDAQ: STTK), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potential first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided recent business highlights. “We are very excited to begin Phase 2 clinical development with SL-325 in both Crohn’s disease and hidradenitis suppurativa. We believe these two studies will allow direct comparisons with the TL1A antibody class and evaluate the efficacy that may be left on the table due to the potential immunogenicity liabilities of TL1A antibodies,” said Taylor Schreiber, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Shattuck. “In addition, SL-846 has demonstrated a compelling profile in preclinical studies, and we expect to share initial Phase 1 clinical data for what we expect to be a first-in-class DR3 by IL-23 receptor blocking antibody in 2027.” DR3 Program Development in 2026 Shattuck is advancing a pipeline of DR3-targeted monoclonal and bispecific antibody product candidates for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Recent updates and anticipated upcoming milestones include: SL-325 Shattuck’s lead clinical-stage product candidate, SL-325, is a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody for the treatment of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), and other inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Phase 1 clinical trial results demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability, potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity with an antidrug antibody rate of 3.7%, and highly durable inhibition of TL1A binding to DR3 that may enable quarterly maintenance dosing. Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate three dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 232 patients, randomized 1:1:1:1. Primary endpoint is endoscopic response at 12 weeks. These data are expected in the first half of 2028. Announced plans to initiate the RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa, with trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. HS is the second Phase 2 indication for SL-325 and expands development beyond IBD. Submitted an Investigational New Drug (IND) application to the FDA in October 2026. Designed RECEPTIVE-HS1 as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating two dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 150 patients, randomized 1:1:1. Primary endpoint is HiSCR50 response at Week 16, with data expected in the first half of 2028. Appointed Shoba Ravichandran, M.D., as Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, to lead the clinical development of SL-325 in HS. Dr. Ravichandran brings more than 20 years of drug development experience, including leading the global approval of Cosentyx in HS at Novartis. SL-846 Shattuck’s lead bispecific product candidate, SL-846, is a potentially first-in-class, half-life extended DR3 x IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking antibody for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Presented preliminary preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from the GLP toxicology study in non-human primates, which showed the following: Well tolerated through the top dose of 100 mg/kg. No evidence of DR3 or IL-23R agonism. Full and durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3, and complete blockade of IL-23 signaling. Data from the NHP study support potential quarterly subcutaneous dosing in humans. NHP and in silico analyses suggest that SL-846 may have a superior immunogenicity profile to TL1A directed bispecific antibodies; projected human anti-drug antibody rate of between 8-12%. Shattuck expects to initiate a Phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial of SL-846 and report initial data in 2027. Upcoming Events Shattuck plans to participate in the following upcoming events. About SL-325 SL-325 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) blocking antibody designed to achieve a complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A pathway. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrated high affinity binding and superior activity over TL1A antibodies, and provided a data-driven rationale for targeting the TNF receptor, DR3, versus its ligand, TL1A. SL-325 is a fully Fc-silenced, fully human immunoglobulin G monoclonal antibody. In a Phase 1 clinical trial, SL-325 demonstrated a favorable safety profile, a potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity profile, no evidence of residual DR3 agonism, and provided durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3 at low doses. SL-325 is being evaluated in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with Crohn’s disease, with data from the induction portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028. We also expect to evaluate SL-325 in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa, with data from the primary treatment portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028. About SL-846 SL-846 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) by IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking bispecific antibody designed to achieve complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A and IL-23/IL-23R pathways. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrate high affinity binding to both DR3 and IL-23R, with equivalent or superior in vitro potency in comparison to benchmark IL-23 controls (sequence equivalents of risankizumab and icotrokinra) in a variety of preclinical assays. SL-846 is an Fc-silenced, half-life extended, fully human immunoglobulin G bispecific antibody that has been evaluated for safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and pharmacodynamics in an IND-enabling GLP toxicology study in non-human primates. – Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in Crohn’s disease; 12-week induction data expected in the first half of 2028 – – Announced RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in hidradenitis suppurativa; trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 – – Presented preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from a chronic toxicology study in non-human primates – AUSTIN, Texas and DURHAM, N.C., Nov.  05, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shattuck Labs, Inc. (Shattuck or the Company) (NASDAQ: STTK), a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potential first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases, today reported financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026 and provided recent business highlights. “We are very excited to begin Phase 2 clinical development with SL-325 in both Crohn’s disease and hidradenitis suppurativa. We believe these two studies will allow direct comparisons with the TL1A antibody class and evaluate the efficacy that may be left on the table due to the potential immunogenicity liabilities of TL1A antibodies,” said Taylor Schreiber, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Shattuck. “In addition, SL-846 has demonstrated a compelling profile in preclinical studies, and we expect to share initial Phase 1 clinical data for what we expect to be a first-in-class DR3 by IL-23 receptor blocking antibody in 2027.” DR3 Program Development in 2026 Shattuck is advancing a pipeline of DR3-targeted monoclonal and bispecific antibody product candidates for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Recent updates and anticipated upcoming milestones include: SL-325 Shattuck’s lead clinical-stage product candidate, SL-325, is a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody for the treatment of Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), and other inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Phase 1 clinical trial results demonstrated favorable safety and tolerability, potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity with an antidrug antibody rate of 3.7%, and highly durable inhibition of TL1A binding to DR3 that may enable quarterly maintenance dosing. Initiated the RECEPTIVE-CD1 Phase 2b clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderately-to-severely active Crohn's disease. Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial designed to evaluate three dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 232 patients, randomized 1:1:1:1. Primary endpoint is endoscopic response at 12 weeks. These data are expected in the first half of 2028. Announced plans to initiate the RECEPTIVE-HS1 Phase 2 clinical trial of SL-325 in patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa, with trial initiation expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. HS is the second Phase 2 indication for SL-325 and expands development beyond IBD. Submitted an Investigational New Drug (IND) application to the FDA in October 2026. Designed RECEPTIVE-HS1 as a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 clinical trial evaluating two dose levels of SL-325 compared with placebo in approximately 150 patients, randomized 1:1:1. Primary endpoint is HiSCR50 response at Week 16, with data expected in the first half of 2028. Appointed Shoba Ravichandran, M.D., as Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, to lead the clinical development of SL-325 in HS. Dr. Ravichandran brings more than 20 years of drug development experience, including leading the global approval of Cosentyx in HS at Novartis. SL-846 Shattuck’s lead bispecific product candidate, SL-846, is a potentially first-in-class, half-life extended DR3 x IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking antibody for the treatment of inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Presented preliminary preclinical data for SL-846 at UEG Week 2026, including data from the GLP toxicology study in non-human primates, which showed the following: Well tolerated through the top dose of 100 mg/kg. No evidence of DR3 or IL-23R agonism. Full and durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3, and complete blockade of IL-23 signaling. Data from the NHP study support potential quarterly subcutaneous dosing in humans. NHP and in silico analyses suggest that SL-846 may have a superior immunogenicity profile to TL1A directed bispecific antibodies; projected human anti-drug antibody rate of between 8-12%. Shattuck expects to initiate a Phase 1 healthy volunteer clinical trial of SL-846 and report initial data in 2027. Upcoming Events Shattuck plans to participate in the following upcoming events. About SL-325
SL-325 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) blocking antibody designed to achieve a complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A pathway. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrated high affinity binding and superior activity over TL1A antibodies, and provided a data-driven rationale for targeting the TNF receptor, DR3, versus its ligand, TL1A. SL-325 is a fully Fc-silenced, fully human immunoglobulin G monoclonal antibody. In a Phase 1 clinical trial, SL-325 demonstrated a favorable safety profile, a potentially best-in-mechanism immunogenicity profile, no evidence of residual DR3 agonism, and provided durable blockade of TL1A binding to DR3 at low doses. SL-325 is being evaluated in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with Crohn’s disease, with data from the induction portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028. We also expect to evaluate SL-325 in a Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with hidradenitis suppurativa, with data from the primary treatment portion of the trial expected in the first half of 2028.
About SL-846
SL-846 is a potentially first-in-class Death Receptor 3 (DR3) by IL-23 receptor (IL-23R) blocking bispecific antibody designed to achieve complete and durable blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A and IL-23/IL-23R pathways. Shattuck’s preclinical studies demonstrate high affinity binding to both DR3 and IL-23R, with equivalent or superior in vitro potency in comparison to benchmark IL-23 controls (sequence equivalents of risankizumab and icotrokinra) in a variety of preclinical assays. SL-846 is an Fc-silenced, half-life extended, fully human immunoglobulin G bispecific antibody that has been evaluated for safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and pharmacodynamics in an IND-enabling GLP toxicology study in non-human primates.

About Shattuck Labs, Inc.
Shattuck Labs, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of potentially first-in-class monoclonal and bispecific DR3 blocking antibodies for the treatment of patients with inflammatory and immune-mediated diseases. Shattuck’s expertise in protein engineering and the development of novel TNF receptor therapeutics come together in its lead program, SL-325, a potentially first-in-class DR3 blocking antibody designed to achieve a more complete blockade of the clinically validated DR3/TL1A pathway. The Company has offices in both Austin, Texas and Durham, North Carolina. For more information, please visit: www.ShattuckLabs.com.

The company’s managerial employees and their closely associated persons have given Genmab A/S power of attorney on their behalf to publish trading in Genmab shares by the company’s managerial employees and their closely associated persons. About Genmab Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn , X , Facebook and Instagram . Contact: Marisol Peron, Senior Vice President, Global Communications & Corporate Affairs T: +1 609 524 0065; E: mmp@genmab.com Andrew Carlsen, Vice President, Head of Investor Relations T: +45 3377 9558; E: acn@genmab.com The Company Announcement contains forward looking statements. Actual results or performance may differ materially from any future results or performance expressed or implied by such statements. The important factors that could cause our actual results or performance to differ materially include, among others, risks associated with preclinical and clinical development of products, uncertainties related to the outcome and conduct of clinical trials including unforeseen safety issues, uncertainties related to product manufacturing, the lack of market acceptance of our products, our inability to manage growth, the competitive environment in relation to our business area and markets, our inability to attract and retain suitably qualified personnel, the unenforceability or lack of protection of our patents and proprietary rights, our relationships with affiliated entities, changes and developments in technology which may render our products or technologies obsolete, and other factors. November 13, 2026 07:00 ET | Source: DelveInsight Business Research LLP DelveInsight Business Research LLP New York, USA, Nov.  13, 2026  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Antithrombotic Drugs Market to Reach USD 89.4 Billion by 2034, Driven by Anticoagulants and Rising Cardiovascular Disease Burden | DelveInsight The global antithrombotic drugs market was valued at USD 46.8 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 89.4 billion by 2034, according to DelveInsight's latest Antithrombotic Drugs Market Insights report. The market is expected to grow at approximately 8% CAGR during the forecast period, driven by the increasing burden of cardiovascular diseases, atrial fibrillation, ischemic stroke, and venous thromboembolism. Anticoagulants accounted for 59% of the global market in 2025, making them the largest drug class, while oral antithrombotic therapies represented 66% of market revenue. North America led the global market with a 44% revenue share. Looking ahead, the emergence of Factor XI/XIa inhibitors, evolving generic competition, and changing treatment and reimbursement patterns are expected to influence the competitive landscape. DelveInsight’s Antithrombotic Drugs Market Insights report provides the current and forecast market analysis, individual leading antithrombotic drugs companies’ market shares, challenges, antithrombotic drugs market drivers, barriers, trends, and key antithrombotic drugs companies in the market. Request a free sample page to know the full forecast of the antithrombotic drugs market size 2034 @ https://www.delveinsight.com/report-store/antithrombotic-drugs-market Himanshu Agnihotri, Project Manager of Healthcare Consulting at DelveInsight, said that the market continues to be dominated by direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), owing to their predictable pharmacological profiles, convenient oral administration, fewer dietary restrictions, and reduced need for routine coagulation monitoring compared with traditional vitamin K antagonists. Additionally, ongoing clinical research focused on developing safer anticoagulants with improved bleeding profiles, specific reversal agents, and novel mechanisms of action is expected to create new growth opportunities. Key Factors Contributing to the Rise in Growth of the Antithrombotic Drugs Market Increasing Prevalence of Cardiovascular Diseases: The rising incidence of cardiovascular disorders, including coronary artery disease, atrial fibrillation, myocardial infarction, and stroke, is significantly driving demand for antithrombotic drugs. These medications play a critical role in preventing thrombus formation and reducing the risk of cardiovascular complications. Growing Burden of Venous Thromboembolism (VTE): The increasing prevalence of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), particularly among hospitalized patients, elderly individuals, and patients undergoing major surgeries, is supporting market expansion. Growing awareness regarding thrombosis prevention is further encouraging the adoption of anticoagulant therapies. Rising Geriatric Population: The expanding global elderly population is contributing to increased demand for antithrombotic drugs, as aging is associated with a higher risk of atrial fibrillation, ischemic stroke, and other thromboembolic disorders. This demographic trend is strengthening the need for long-term anticoagulation and antiplatelet treatment. Advancements in Antithrombotic Drug Development: Continuous innovation in anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents is improving treatment efficacy, safety, and patient convenience. The introduction of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), including factor Xa inhibitors and direct thrombin inhibitors, has enhanced treatment options by reducing monitoring requirements and simplifying dosing regimens. Increasing Adoption of Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs): The growing preference for DOACs over traditional vitamin K antagonists, such as warfarin, is supporting market growth. Their predictable pharmacological profiles, fewer dietary restrictions, and reduced need for routine coagulation monitoring have improved treatment accessibility and patient adherence. Expansion of Surgical and Interventional Procedures: The increasing number of cardiovascular surgeries, orthopedic procedures, and percutaneous coronary interventions is driving demand for antithrombotic medications. These drugs are extensively used to prevent perioperative thrombosis and reduce the risk of clot-related complications following surgical and interventional procedures. Growing Awareness of Thrombosis Prevention and Management: Increased awareness among healthcare professionals and patients regarding the consequences of untreated thromboembolic conditions is encouraging early diagnosis and preventive treatment. Educational initiatives, screening programs, and improved clinical guidelines are supporting the wider utilization of antithrombotic therapies. Improving Healthcare Infrastructure and Access to Treatment: Investments in healthcare infrastructure, particularly across emerging economies, are improving access to cardiovascular diagnostics, specialized treatment facilities, and pharmaceutical products. Expanding healthcare coverage and improving affordability are further facilitating the adoption of antithrombotic medications. Increasing Research and Development Investments: Pharmaceutical companies are investing significantly in developing novel anticoagulants and antiplatelet agents with improved efficacy and lower bleeding risks. Ongoing clinical trials targeting unmet needs in thrombosis prevention and cardiovascular disease management are expected to create additional growth opportunities. Expanding Applications of Antithrombotic Therapies: Antithrombotic drugs are increasingly being utilized across a broad range of indications, including atrial fibrillation, acute coronary syndromes, stroke prevention, VTE management, and thrombosis prevention following medical procedures. The expanding clinical applications of these therapies are contributing to sustained market demand. Get a sneak peek at the antithrombotic drugs market dynamics @ Antithrombotic Drugs Market Forecast Regional Antithrombotic Drugs Market Insights North America North America captured 44% of global antithrombotic drugs market revenue in 2025, securing the largest regional market share worldwide. This leadership is attributed to the high prevalence of atrial fibrillation and cardiovascular disorders, widespread adoption of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), comprehensive reimbursement frameworks, and the strong presence of major pharmaceutical companies such as Bristol Myers Squibb, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson, and Eli Lilly. The United States represents the world's largest DOAC prescribing market, benefiting from established clinical guidelines and extensive payer formulary coverage. However, evolving patent expirations, including generic rivaroxaban entry following the 2025 U.S. patent expiry and anticipated generic apixaban availability from 2028, are gradually transforming competitive dynamics and pricing structures. Originator companies are responding through direct-to-patient initiatives and product life-cycle management strategies to preserve market share. Additionally, substantial surgical procedure volumes, population aging, and an advanced clinical-trial ecosystem supporting next-generation Factor XI/XIa inhibitors continue to reinforce North America's market leadership throughout the forecast period. Europe Europe accounted for a significant share of the global antithrombotic drugs market in 2025, supported by the high prevalence of cardiovascular diseases, an aging population, widespread adoption of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), and well-established healthcare systems across Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Italy, and Spain. The region benefits from comprehensive healthcare coverage, established clinical guidelines, and strong adoption of anticoagulant and antiplatelet therapies for the management of atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and ischemic cardiovascular conditions. Germany represents a major regional market, supported by its advanced healthcare infrastructure, high pharmaceutical expenditure, and extensive cardiovascular treatment capabilities, while the United Kingdom and France benefit from established reimbursement frameworks and evidence-based prescribing practices. However, increasing generic competition following patent expirations of key anticoagulants, including rivaroxaban and apixaban, is progressively reshaping regional pricing dynamics and market competition. Pharmaceutical companies are increasingly emphasizing product differentiation, lifecycle management, and the development of next-generation anticoagulants with improved safety profiles, particularly Factor XI/XIa inhibitors, to address the limitations associated with conventional anticoagulant therapies. Additionally, rising cardiovascular disease burden, growing demand for stroke prevention, increasing surgical procedure volumes, and continued clinical research activities are expected to sustain Europe's contribution to the global Antithrombotic Drugs market throughout the forecast period. Asia-Pacific Asia-Pacific is projected to register the fastest growth in the antithrombotic drugs market, supported by increasing cardiovascular disease prevalence, population expansion and aging, rising healthcare expenditure, and improved diagnosis and treatment of atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism across China, Japan, India, South Korea, and Australia. China is strengthening domestic DOAC manufacturing capabilities while expanding reimbursement access, whereas Japan benefits from a well-established anticoagulant market and an increasingly aging population. India presents substantial growth opportunities through its large, underserved patient population and cost-efficient generic and branded-generic pharmaceutical manufacturing ecosystem. Increasing awareness of thromboembolic disorders, expanding hospital and cardiovascular care infrastructure, and growing regional production of generic anticoagulants and antiplatelet therapies are further supporting market penetration. Collectively, the region's substantial disease burden, demographic transition, and ongoing healthcare infrastructure development position Asia-Pacific as a major contributor to incremental market growth over the forecast period. To know more about why North America is leading the antithrombotic drugs market, get a snapshot of the Antithrombotic Drugs Market Trends Recent Developmental Activities in the Antithrombotic Drugs Market In 2026, Bristol Myers Squibb and Johnson & Johnson reported final Phase 3 LIBREXIA ACS results at the European Society of Cardiology Congress showing the Factor XIa inhibitor milvexian did not reduce cardiovascular events when added to standard antiplatelet therapy after acute coronary syndrome, following the trial's discontinuation for futility in November 2025. In May 2026, Bristol Myers Squibb and Pfizer saw Eliquis (apixaban) lose regulatory market exclusivity across the European Union, opening the region to generic apixaban competition. In 2026, Bayer continued advancing its oral Factor XIa inhibitor asundexian in ischemic stroke prevention following earlier discontinuation of a separate Phase 3 atrial fibrillation trial on comparative efficacy grounds. What are Antithrombotic Drugs? Antithrombotic drugs are a class of medications that prevent the formation of blood clots (thrombi) or inhibit their growth, thereby reducing the risk of thromboembolic complications such as stroke, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). These drugs act by interfering with different components of the blood coagulation process and are broadly classified into three major categories: anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, and thrombolytic drugs. Anticoagulants, including heparin, warfarin, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), inhibit the coagulation cascade and prevent fibrin clot formation, while antiplatelet agents such as aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet aggregation and thrombus formation, particularly in arterial circulation. Thrombolytic agents, including alteplase and tenecteplase, actively dissolve existing blood clots by promoting fibrinolysis. Antithrombotic therapies are widely used in the prevention and management of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, as well as venous thromboembolic diseases, although their use requires careful monitoring due to the potential risk of bleeding complications. What are Antithrombotic Drugs? Antithrombotic drugs are a class of medications that prevent the formation of blood clots (thrombi) or inhibit their growth, thereby reducing the risk of thromboembolic complications such as stroke, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). These drugs act by interfering with different components of the blood coagulation process and are broadly classified into three major categories: anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, and thrombolytic drugs. Anticoagulants, including heparin, warfarin, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), inhibit the coagulation cascade and prevent fibrin clot formation, while antiplatelet agents such as aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet aggregation and thrombus formation, particularly in arterial circulation. Thrombolytic agents, including alteplase and tenecteplase, actively dissolve existing blood clots by promoting fibrinolysis. Antithrombotic therapies are widely used in the prevention and management of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, as well as venous thromboembolic diseases, although their use requires careful monitoring due to the potential risk of bleeding complications. What are Antithrombotic Drugs? Antithrombotic drugs are a class of medications that prevent the formation of blood clots (thrombi) or inhibit their growth, thereby reducing the risk of thromboembolic complications such as stroke, myocardial infarction, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE). These drugs act by interfering with different components of the blood coagulation process and are broadly classified into three major categories: anticoagulants, antiplatelet agents, and thrombolytic drugs. Anticoagulants, including heparin, warfarin, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), inhibit the coagulation cascade and prevent fibrin clot formation, while antiplatelet agents such as aspirin and clopidogrel reduce platelet aggregation and thrombus formation, particularly in arterial circulation. Thrombolytic agents, including alteplase and tenecteplase, actively dissolve existing blood clots by promoting fibrinolysis. Antithrombotic therapies are widely used in the prevention and management of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders, as well as venous thromboembolic diseases, although their use requires careful monitoring due to the potential risk of bleeding complications.
